newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SFE WHEAT RISES FURTHER TO BUCK CHICAGO TREND.
newsitem.headline: SFE WHEAT RISES FURTHER TO BUCK CHICAGO TREND.

text.p: Sydney Futures Exchange (SFE) wheat futures continued to rise on Wednesday despite Chicago's overnight fall on bearish USDA U.S. wheat production figures.
SFE January 1998 sold steady at A$192.00 a tonne, the only contract to trade. Three put options also sold on A$185.00 January 1998 at a A$9.00 premium.
Settlement prices rose virtually across the board, by between A$1.00 and A$7.00 a tonne.
A broker said that SFE wheat futures were responding to local conditions, mainly a rainfall performance which had not fully clinched the crop.
Other brokers pointed to the prospect of tight supplies regardless of precisely how much this season produced.

In overnight news, the USDA increased its forecast for 1997 U.S. wheat production to 2.531 billion bushels from 2.431 billion forecast in July. It cut its production estimates for Argentina, Australia and Canada but sharply boosted its forecast for China and the former Soviet Union.
The USDA's latest forecast for current season Australian wheat production was pitched at 16.0 million tonnes, down from 18.50 million tonnes in the previous forecast.
This is in roughly line with Australian forecasts.
